name: Rocker arms and VTEC assembly
what: The B16 VTEC valvetrain uses rocker arms to transfer cam-lobe motion to the valves. The VTEC mechanism hydraulically locks selected rocker arms together so the high-lift cam profile can control valve motion.
why: The rocker arms transmit camshaft movement to the valves. VTEC changes which rocker profile controls the valves, allowing the engine to use a different lift and duration behavior when operating conditions call for it.
where: The rocker assemblies sit in the cylinder head between the camshaft lobes and the valve stems, with separate intake and exhaust rocker groups.
installationReason: Fit the rocker assemblies after the camshafts are in position. The model shows three rocker fingers per cylinder on each camshaft row, representing the primary, secondary, and center high-lift rocker arrangement.

guide.overview: The B16 VTEC system uses a set of rocker arms for the intake and exhaust valve groups. The center rocker follows the high-lift cam lobe; the VTEC locking mechanism can couple the rocker group so the high-lift profile controls valve motion.
guide.operation: At lower engine speeds, the primary and secondary rocker fingers follow their respective cam profiles. When the engine management system commands VTEC and sufficient oil pressure is available, a hydraulic pin slides to couple the rocker fingers. The linked group then follows the high-lift cam profile. The exact engagement strategy depends on the B16 variant.
guide.construction: This procedural educational model represents the rocker fingers, cam-contact pads, valve-contact pads, pivot bosses, and a simplified VTEC locking-pin detail. It is not a factory CAD reproduction.
guide.specifications: Exact B16 variant-specific rocker dimensions, pin clearances, oil pressure thresholds, engagement rpm, and service limits are intentionally omitted because they have not been verified against a matching Honda service manual.
guide.inspection: Inspect rocker contact surfaces, pivots, locking pins, and oil passages for scoring, wear, sticking, or blocked oil feed. Confirm variant-specific inspection limits and VTEC test procedures using the correct Honda service information.
guide.failureModes: Possible issues include worn rocker contact surfaces, sticking or worn locking pins, restricted oil feed, and failure to engage VTEC. Symptoms and diagnostic thresholds depend on the exact B16 variant.
